title: Marangoni swimmer-spread loop 3 (negative): short-lived rich food patches on top of the sink discs reward swimming speed, not distance per cycle. The mar-60 kind fixes in the escape arm on seed 502 (trait mean 60 vs 46.7 in the twin) because it swims 1.6x faster and divides 1.9x sooner, so its distance per cycle does not rise, and the M-gate share stays at 0/10 and 1/13 (twin 2/20, 1/11)
summary: The loop-1 world (c45's mar 20/40/60 ladder with in-run mutation, all founders mar 40, growing sink discs) plus food flashes: 12-px patches open for 100 t, one per 25 t, where the chemostat rate is 5x (same target, no nucleation). E and identical-event twin on fresh seeds 502 and 503. The trait mean ends higher in E than in the twin on both seeds (60 vs 46.7; 36 vs 20, the twin down to 2 bodies), but the share of dividing rods that swim 3 of their own lengths with the rear tip advancing is 0-10% in both arms and the selection gradient on distance per cycle is -0.29 and -0.04 in E. Pooled over E, mar-60 dividing rods swim at path speed 0.38 vs 0.24 (mar 40) but divide after 125 t vs 235 t, so their median distance per cycle (1.80 rod lengths) does not exceed mar 40's (2.00); speed vs cycle Spearman -0.39. Food patches did not enlarge the populations (2-8 bodies at the end). In this world an environment that pays for moving also shortens the cycle, so selecting the Marangoni coefficient does not select the challenge's capability.

finding.operator: short-lived rich supply patches (local 5x chemostat rate) with the heritable Marangoni ladder and growing sink discs
finding.control: identical-event twin (MARS 40/40/40) on the same seeds 502 and 503
finding.result: trait mean T=2000: E 60.0 / 36.0, twin 46.7 / 20.0; M passers E 0/10, 1/13, twin 2/20, 1/11; D gradient E -0.29, -0.04; mar-60 vs mar-40 dividing rods in E: path speed 0.38 vs 0.24, cycle 125 vs 235 t, median D 1.80 vs 2.00
